title: Rapid Onramp Adoption Lab — engagement outline and pricing sketch
content:
Context and objective:

This note is a working sketch for a short-form 'Adoption Lab' engagement with a mid-market SaaS customer who wants to evaluate integrating real-time recommendations and contextual chat into their agent console. The goal: provide a fast turn-on POC that demonstrates production-feasible latency (p95 < 300ms), predictable cost estimates, and a clear migration path from hosted API -> dedicated capacity. This doc balances scope with a tight 6-week timeline so we can surface integration risks early.

High-level success criteria:
- Functional: integrated recommendation API + contextual chat flow launched against a representative dataset (10k user events).
- Performance: end-to-end 95th percentile latency < 300ms for common queries at target QPS of 5 concurrent users.
- Cost visibility: per-user and per-session unit economics established with two candidate serving configurations (hosted optimized + dedicated baseline).
- Operability: runbook for failover and telemetry hooks in Console implemented (traces, token breakdowns).

Core delivery items (what Redwood delivers):
1) 2-week Discovery + Design workshop (onsite or virtual) — consolidated findings and a prioritized integration plan.
2) 4-week Build & Validate sprint: connector code, prompt templates, end-to-end tests, and a small eval harness (synthetic and sampled real sessions).
3) Performance tuning pass: batching/quantization suggestions and one model variant recommendation for low-cost baseline.
4) Short ops package: runbook, rollout checklist, and dashboard templates for Console (latency/cost by route).
5) Handover: code repo with CI, deployment example (Terraform + container), and 2 hours of knowledge-transfer + 1 day of follow-up office hours.

Scope boundaries (out of scope unless explicitly added):
- Large scale dataset ingestion or custom model training/finetuning.
- Full enterprise compliance packaging (FedRAMP/PCL) — we can offer Private deployment scoping separately.
- Long‑term managed services beyond the 6-week engagement.

Assumptions:
- Customer provides representative sample dataset (10k events) and a staging endpoint for their console integration (API keys / service account access) within first 3 business days.
- Customer will assign one technical PM and one backend engineer as points of contact.
- Model choices: we will start with Redwood-hosted open model X (gptx-8b-optimized) and evaluate a quantized variant for dedicated baseline.

Proposed timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): contract & scoping signoff, access provisioning.
- Week 1–2: Discovery + 2-day on-site workshop (agenda below), architecture design, test corpus collection. Deliverable: Design brief + integration plan.
- Week 3–4: Implement connectors, prompt engineering, first pass CI tests. Deliverable: Staging demo.
- Week 5: Load/perf pass, tuning (batching, caching), cost analysis. Deliverable: Performance report + recommendations.
- Week 6: Handover, runbook, and executive demo. Deliverable: Final artifacts + knowledge transfer.

Workshop agenda (2-day target):
Day 1 — Product & integration:
- 9:00 intro, goals, success criteria (30m)
- 9:30 mapping existing console flows + data availability (90m)
- 11:00 breakouts: recommendation API spec & chat handoff points (60m)
- 13:00 lunch
- 14:00 prompt templates and failure modes (90m)
- 15:30 telemetry and rollout strategy (60m)
- 16:30 action items + owner mapping (30m)

Day 2 — Ops & performance:
- 9:00 serving topology overview (hosted vs dedicated) (45m)
- 9:45 batching/caching patterns and KV cache strategy (60m)
- 11:00 quantization and kernel compatibility checklist (45m)
- 12:00 lunch
- 13:00 perf SLOs and chaos/fallback tests (90m)
- 14:30 runbook drafting session (60m)
- 15:30 pricing walkthrough and next steps (45m)

Roles & responsibilities:
- Redwood SE lead (Maya) — overall delivery, architecture, perf tuning.
- Redwood infra/serving SME (Carlos) — batching, KV caching, dedicated sizing.
- Redwood product analyst (Evelyn) — cost modeling and dashboards.
- Customer PM/engineer(s) — data access, integration, validation.

Acceptance criteria (to transition to final deliverable):
- Demo checklist passed: recommendation endpoint responds with contextual data and passes integrity tests.
- Performance: synthetic 95th percentile latency < 300ms for baseline request profile.
- Cost model created with per-session and monthly projection for 10k MAU, with two serving configurations.
- Runbook reviewed and signed off by customer engineer.

Pricing & packaging (sketch) — choose one of these engagement options:
Option A — Rapid Onramp (recommended for early adopters)
- Fixed-price Discovery (2 weeks): $18,000 (deliverable: design brief + integration plan)
- Build & Validate (4 weeks): Time & Materials; estimated 160 engineer hours @ $225/hr = $36,000 (expected range $30k–$45k)
- Performance tuning & ops package: fixed $8,000
- Total estimated: $62,000 (range $56k–$71k)
- Optional add-on: Dedicated baseline sizing and initial capacity reservation: one-time $12,000 (capacity engineering + infra provisioning)

Option B — Accelerated Fixed SOW
- 6-week fixed SOW: $92,000 (includes Discovery, Build, Perf, Ops, and 2 days onsite)
- Includes one complimentary month of Basic Dedicated trial (customer pays infra usage)
- Good when the customer prefers a predictable fixed cost and limited scoping overhead.

Operational cost guidance (example outputs from our cost model)
- Hosted optimized variant: estimated token cost $0.00035 per generated token; for typical session (prompt 400 tokens, generated 200 tokens) = ~ $0.105/session.
- Dedicated baseline (quantized model): amortized infra + ops estimate ~ $0.045/session at 10k MAU (high variance depending on request distribution).
- Recommendation: run both in parallel for 2–4 weeks and compare real-world unit economics.

Contract & procurement notes:
- Standard Redwood SOW template applies (we will attach terms appendix).
- Payment schedule: 30% on signature, 50% at mid-point milestone (end of week 3), 20% on final delivery.
- Travel: onsite days (if chosen) billed at cost plus per-diem.

Risks & mitigations:
- Data access delays — mitigation: require staging credentials within 3 business days of kickoff, otherwise swap to synthetic corpus and add time for re-run once data available.
- Unexpected model compatibility with customer tokenization — mitigation: early compatibility checks in week 1 and fallback to alternate model variant.
- Perf gap at QPS peak — mitigation: emergency tuning sprint + temporary scaling policy to hosted burst.

Open questions for customer to answer before kickoff:
- Can you provide a representative 10k-row session dataset, sanitized, by kickoff?
- Which cloud region(s) must we target for latency (US-West, EU)?
- Any hard constraints on tokens per session or monthly spend caps?

Next steps (internal)
- Turn this sketch into a short SOW doc (2–3 pages) and attach to a procurement checklist. Owner: Maya — target 2024-05-06.
- Pre-workshop: create data ingestion template and minimal test harness. Owner: Carlos — target 2024-05-03.
- Cost model: Evelyn to produce two scenario dashboards (hosted vs dedicated) and share with customer prior to workshop. Target: 2024-05-07.

Notes to self / working items (informal):
- Consider adding a short 'fallback flow' demo that shows graceful degradation to smaller model variant — useful for execs.
- Track potential dedicated pricing credits we can offer for the POC to reduce friction.
- Confirm whether KMS integration is required; if yes, add Private deployment scoping addendum.

Attachments (to include in final SOW):
- Design brief template
- Performance checklist and synthetic load script
- Runbook skeleton
- Pricing scenarios spreadsheet

-- end of sketch --
